Ibrahim Khan: hey all, day 2 here. quick org question: when i request access (buckets, creds, kube), who should i CC besides my manager? onboarding doc is vague about who needs to be in the loop.
Nina Alvarez: welcome! always cc your manager + team lead. platform/infra likes to have the request linked to a ticket and the service OWNER. so include the repo OWNER (check infra/OWNERS.md) and the service alias (e.g., @team-embed).
Samir Patel: adding: for anything that touches prod data also cc privacy@ and security@. people-ops-bot will flag contractor requests that need extra approvals.
Ibrahim Khan: good call. what's the fast path if an owner is unresponsive and it's blocking a demo?
Nina Alvarez: if OWNER doesn't respond in ~30m, ping #eng-oncall and post the ticket link. oncall can set a temporary owner or approve timeboxed creds for emergencies. make sure you include a rollback plan in the ticket.
Samir Patel: for non-urgent housekeeping (stale OWNERS, missing CODEOWNERS) open a PR to update it and @mention the proposed owner. if unsure who to pick, put @platform as fallback.
people-ops-bot: Reminder: Manager approval required for any long-lived credentials. Contractors need additional People Ops approval.
oncall-bot: Incident flow reminder: for production-impacting access or quota issues, open a ticket with "prod-impact" tag and page eng-oncall.
Ibrahim Khan: thanks! last thing: who owns billing alerts and cost-related quotas? i once got paged and had no idea who to CC.
Samir Patel: FinOps owns billing alerts (finops@redwood-infer.com). For quota-related limits that affect deploys, Platform owns quotas; FinOps owns billing thresholds. Include both if cost + infra are involved.
Nina Alvarez: also FYI: most teams keep an "oncall + owners" section in their README. search the service repo for "OWNERS" or "oncall".
Ibrahim Khan: perfect, saving this thread for other new hires. much appreciated :pray:
Nina Alvarez: welcome aboard! DM me if you want a quick walkthrough of the OWNERS pattern.
